raw_statement_observations.observation: n is a fixed positive integer greater than1. Harmonicity on an open set means C2 and zero coordinate Laplacian. Harmonicity on a not necessarily open set E is defined by existence of a harmonic extension to an open set containing E.
Functions are complex-valued by default. The real-valued theorem is a scalar specialization; the original statement is not limited to real functions.
The overbar in the theorem is visible: harmonicity is required on the closed ball. The conclusion is u(a)=integral_S u(a+r zeta)d sigma(zeta), with S the unit sphere and sigma normalized to mass1.
The proof first assumes n>2 and reduces to the unit ball without writing the affine transport details.
For n=2 the source instructs replacing |x|^(2-n) by log|x|; it does not print the resulting boundary computation.
